title: AS2 compiler: fold unary minus on numeric literals into direct negative push
description:
The compiler emits `Push int(0)` + `Push f64(v)` + `ActionSubtract` for unary minus applied to a numeric literal (e.g. `-.5`, `-0.5`, `-180`). This is semantically correct but generates 3 extra instructions per negative literal vs. pushing the negative value directly.

Found by: analysis of the MagSave game script (task 1057 analysis trace). Example: `_root.meteor.grav = -.5;` emits 10 opcodes instead of the optimal 7.

Root cause: `compileUnaryExpr` for operator `'-'` always emits `pushInt(0) + compileExpr(operand) + Subtract`, even when the operand is a constant Literal. It should short-circuit when `operand.type === 'Literal' && typeof operand.value === 'number'` and instead call `pushNumber(-operand.value)` directly.

Fix: In `compileUnaryExpr`, case `'-'`: check if operand is a Literal number, and if so emit `this.pushNumber(-operand.value)` directly. Otherwise fall back to the current `0 - operand` pattern.

This is a perf/size optimization only — there are no known correctness failures from the current behavior. Priority: low.
